texts.preamble: M/S. Firmenich Aromatics Production ... vs Vidya S B, Asst. Director, Desi. Officer ... on 16 October, 2025 Author: Revati Mohite Dere Bench: Revati Mohite Dere 903.Wp-13588-2025 In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay Civil Appellate Jurisdiction Civil Writ Petition No.13588 Of 2025 M/s. Firmenich Aromatics Production (India) Private Limited ... Petitioner V/s.
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition seeking quashing of the order dated 9th October 2025 passed M/S. Firmenich Aromatics Production ... vs Vidya S B, Asst. Director, Desi. Officer ... on 16 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123725018/ 1 by the (Assistant 903.WP-13588-2025 Director), Designated officer and Central licensing authority - Daman Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli FSSAI, Western region, Mumbai. By the impugned Order the petitioner was prohibited from selling the articles, namely, (1) Cocoa powder, replacer flavour 1516SPM; and (2) Cocoa powder, replacer flavour 1728SPM under any name/Mode/Brand.
texts.arguments: 2. Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioners contended that the petitioner is carrying out business activities of "Relabeller Substances Added to Food" and "Manufacturer - Substances Added to Food", since last two years; and that the petitioner is doing the business, by obtaining appropriate licenses from the respondent No.1. It is contended by the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner that on the basis of a letter written to the Prime Minister's office regarding the products of the petitioner, the respondent No.2 conducted an inspection of the products of the petitioner in the factory on 8th October 2025. It is further contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that on 9th October 2025, 903.WP-13588-2025 without even waiting for the Food Analyst report, the impugned order was passed by the respondent No.2. It is the contention of the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner that the impugned order is passed in gross defiance of the principles of natural justice. He submits that the petitioner has not contravened any process under the Food Safety Act or the Rules made therein. Learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner further contended that both the manufacturer, that is VKL and the relabeler i.e. the petitioner hold valid, subsisting FSSAI licenses and that the products in question are "Nature - Identical Flavouring Substances". 3. Learned counsel for the respondent supported the impugned judgment and order. She contended that upon scrutiny of the label specimen, brochure, copy, and the composition/ statement of ingredients and other documents, including license of the product, namely Cocoa powder, replacer flavour 1516SPM and Cocoa powder replace flavour 1728SPM, which are manufactured by M/s. VKL Seasoning Private Limited , it was found that the petitioner had no valid license from the respondent. She submits that thus there was violation of the conditions and labelling and display regulations. Learned Counsel for the respondent further contended that there was no valid license for food, business activity of articles in question, nor was there compliance of the conditions of license, safety measures etc. Learned Counsel appearing for the respondent, however, stated that she requires some time to file an affidavit in reply of the respondents. 4. The learned Senior counsel appearing for the petitioner pressed for stay to the impugned order.
